units.title: Holm supply boat busy as contract nears its end
units.author: courier
units.text: The contractor's workboat serving Kittering Holm made an early crossing from Gilliver yesterday morning, loading at the harbour's berth 3 before first light. Harbour users had been asked to keep the berth clear on the final two mornings of the 30-day clearance contract, which ends tomorrow.

units.author: courier
units.text: Onlookers on the harbour wall said the boat went out carrying fuel drums and returned with covered equipment and waste skips. Some took this as a sign that the clearance is close to complete; others noted that fuel was still being sent out. Neither interpretation could be confirmed.

units.author: courier
units.text: The harbourmaster said the contractor had booked the berth for the 29th and 30th and that he had 'not been told of any sailings after that'. He asked the public not to gather on the pontoon approach during loading, for safety reasons.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services did not respond to questions about when the crew are expected to leave the island. A Courier reporter has also asked Ardent Vale Holdings whether any further works are planned on the Holm once the clearance contract ends. The company said it had 'nothing to add at this time'.

units.title: Letters: lamps, ferries and the island
units.author: courier
units.text: A Lisle reader writes to thank the ferry crews 'who have been laughed at in public this month for doing their jobs properly'. She says the night crossings now feel safer than ever with the new lighting, and asks that the Courier 'give the teasing a rest now that one young man has had the decency to own up'.

units.author: courier
units.text: A Gilliver correspondent objects to visitors photographing the harbour front at night. 'The lamps in our windows are not a tourist attraction,' he writes. 'They are a custom older than the Courier, and we would be grateful if people kept their cameras for the lifeboat.'

units.author: courier
units.text: A Tollinby reader asks why the Courier has written so much about Kittering Holm when, in his view, 'a company cutting down its own trees on its own island is not news'. He suggests the paper turn its attention to the state of the Tollinby market car park instead.

units.author: courier
units.text: And a Port Ammet reader writes simply: 'Whoever is working out on the Holm, I hope you are warm and that you get home safely. We can see your lights from our kitchen. Somebody here is thinking of you.' The Courier is happy to print it.

units.title: Live: Port Ammet winter market opens
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:00: The Port Ammet winter market has opened on the harbour square with forty-two stalls, the most in its history. Organisers say the settled weather has brought traders from as far as Weyhaven. There is a queue at the smoked-fish stall already.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 11:00: The council has opened the overflow car park at the ferry terminal. Listeners report the main car park full since half past ten. The Lisle ferry is carrying more foot passengers than usual, and Sound Lines has added a crew member to the gangway.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:30: Our reporter says the busiest stall this year is selling small lamps and lanterns, mostly second-hand, restored by a retired engineer from Tollinby. He says he has sold more in a morning than in the whole of last year's market and has 'no idea why'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:00: The Lisle school choir has sung on the harbour steps, raising money for the new school roof. A collection bucket, one of the actual buckets from the leaking hall, has been passed round. The head teacher says it is 'the first time it's been full of something useful'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:30: Traders are packing up as the light goes, and the market closes at five. Organisers estimate four thousand visitors. The market returns next weekend. That's the end of our live coverage; thank you for all your messages and photos.

units.title: Dock pay talks resume at Weyhaven container port
units.author: weypost
units.text: Talks over night-shift pay at Weyhaven's container port resumed yesterday after a three-week pause. Union representatives say night workers are owed an allowance agreed two years ago but never paid. The port operator says the allowance was 'conditional on productivity measures' that were not met.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A crane driver with twenty years at the port told the Post that the outages earlier this month had 'shown everyone what nights actually cost'. During one outage, he said, staff waited in the dark on the quay for nearly an hour before the backup generators were brought online.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Both sides say they hope for an agreement before the winter timetable begins. A further meeting is scheduled for next week. No industrial action has been proposed.

units.title: City to audit stairwell lighting in tower blocks
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven city council will audit emergency and stairwell lighting in all council-owned tower blocks this winter, following complaints from residents across the city during this month's power cuts. The audit will also invite private landlords to take part voluntarily.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The housing committee chair said residents had reported 'stairwells going dark between floors for hours at a time', and that older residents in particular had stopped using the stairs at night. She cited the recent repairs at Dellow Court, a privately managed block, as an example of a problem 'that should never have taken weeks to fix'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates, which manages Dellow Court, said it 'welcomes any initiative to improve resident safety' and that the faulty timer relay in its building was 'fully resolved'. Residents' groups said they would be watching the audit closely.

units.title: Softwood prices ease as mills report full yards
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Prices for standing softwood in the region eased slightly this month as sawmills reported full log yards ahead of winter. Two mills in the Weyhaven area said they had stopped buying small roundwood until the new year, citing storage limits and lower demand for fencing.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Hardwood remains firm, with good demand for firewood after the outages. One merchant said he had sold 'a winter's worth of logs in a fortnight', mostly to households that had not owned a stove until this year.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Analysts expect prices to recover in spring as construction resumes. Contractors are advised to agree fixed rates for winter thinning work now, before the usual rush in February.

units.title: Short-deadline clearance contracts draw scrutiny
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The forestry contractors' association has said it will publish guidance on 'time-critical clearance contracts' next year, after members raised concerns about jobs that pair very short deadlines with remote sites. The association did not name any contract, but the Kittering Holm clearance has been widely discussed in the trade this month.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Members' concerns include fatigue, the difficulty of evacuating an injured worker from an island without road access, and contracts that make crew transport 'subject to client arrangement'. 'If you can't say how your people get home, you shouldn't sign,' said one association member.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Online claims by a former employee about an earlier Grieve contract further north could not be verified by the Journal; the account that posted them has since been deleted. Grieve Land Services said it had 'an unblemished safety record' and would contribute to the association's guidance.

units.title: Gilliver and Lisle slipways to get permanent lighting
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Permanent lighting will be installed on the slipways at Gilliver and Lisle before the end of the year, the harbour authority has announced. Temporary lights on the Lisle pier office went up this week, and the Gilliver slip will follow once a power supply has been run down the harbour wall.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Gilliver harbourmaster said the work was 'overdue' and that the slipways had been 'too dark for too long, whatever anybody thinks they saw on them'. The cost will be met from the harbour maintenance fund.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Fishermen have welcomed the decision but asked for the lights to be shielded from the water, so they do not dazzle crews approaching the slip at night. The authority says it will consult boat owners on the design.

units.title: Overnight show: record month for listener calls
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound FM's overnight programme has had its busiest month for listener calls since it began, the station says, with more than eleven hundred calls between midnight and five. The station puts the rise down to the power cuts, when many listeners relied on battery radios.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The programme's producer said most callers simply wanted company. 'People ring to say the power's off on their street, or back on, or that they can't sleep,' she said. 'A lot of them just want to hear that someone else is up.' She said the show would keep its extended phone lines through the winter.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Asked about recent online discussion of unusual calls to the programme, the producer said the station 'checks what it can and doesn't broadcast what it can't', and that callers' details are never shared.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, 29th
units.author: met
units.text: Settled. Today: frost and freezing fog patches inland clearing by late morning, then sunny and still. Maximum 6 degrees. Tonight: clear, calm and cold again, frost widespread, minimum minus 4 inland, 0 on the coast. Outlook: high pressure slowly drifting east, staying dry for several days.

units.title: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters, next 24 hours. Wind variable 1 to 3, becoming southeast 3 later. Sea smooth. Fair. Visibility very good, locally poor in sea smoke near dawn. Outlook for the following 24 hours: southeast 3 or 4, slight, fair, good.

units.title: Tide times, Gilliver, 29th
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver tides: high water 05:31 (4.2 m) and 17:52 (4.4 m); low water 11:44 (0.8 m). Next low water 00:10 (0.7 m). Half-tide windows for small landings around 08:40 and 14:50. Spring tides from the 2nd.

units.title: Yellow warning: fog and ice, inland, tonight
units.author: met
units.text: Yellow warning for freezing fog and ice, 23:00 tonight to 10:00 tomorrow, inland areas only, including Brackwater, the reservoir road and the Tollinby road. Visibility may fall below 100 metres in places. Coastal areas and the Sound are expected to stay clear.

units.title: Service update, 29th
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines: all sailings are operating normally today. Extra foot-passenger capacity will be provided on Lisle sailings between 09:00 and 17:00 for the Port Ammet winter market. Vehicle bookings are recommended for the 16:40 from Gilliver.

units.title: Winter timetable from the 3rd
units.author: ferry
units.text: Customer notice: the Sound Lines winter timetable starts on the 3rd. The 22:40 night crossing continues on weekdays and Saturdays; there will be no Sunday night crossing until spring. The first Lisle sailing moves to 07:15. Printed timetables are available at all terminals.

units.title: Network summary: no unplanned interruptions
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op network summary: no unplanned interruptions were recorded anywhere on the network in the last 72 hours. Insulator replacement continues on the Brackwater and Carrow Point spans during daylight hours, under live-working procedures. No customer interruptions are expected from this work.

units.author: power
units.text: Reminder: the planned interruption in Tollinby north (Mill Lane, Orchard Rise and the industrial estate) goes ahead tomorrow, the 30th, from 09:00 to 13:00. The weather forecast is favourable. Our crew will be on site from 08:30.

units.title: Planning applications received this week
units.author: council
units.text: Planning applications received: two-storey rear extension, 14 Quay Street, Port Ammet; change of use from shop to café, Market Row, Tollinby; replacement boathouse doors, Lisle; woodland thinning, Brackwater estate (amended plans). Comments may be made online for 21 days from the date of this notice.

units.title: Grit bins refilled
units.author: council
units.text: Grit bins on hills and at school entrances in Tollinby, Brackwater and Port Ammet have been refilled ahead of further frosts. Residents may use the grit on public pavements and paths. Please do not take grit for private driveways; supplies are limited.

units.author: council
units.text: Update: mains flushing in Lisle village was completed at 14:20 today. Any remaining discolouration should clear within a few hours. If your water is still not clear by tomorrow morning, please contact the council's water line.

units.title: Vessel movements: Gilliver to Kittering Holm
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. A contractor's workboat will make crossings between Gilliver harbour and the Kittering Holm landing stage on the mornings of the 29th and 30th, departing around 06:30. Mariners are asked to give the vessel room while it manoeuvres at the landing stage. No further movements have been notified.

units.title: Lifeboat exercise, Gilliver approaches
units.author: coast
units.text: The Gilliver inshore lifeboat will carry out a training exercise in the harbour approaches on the 30th between 10:00 and 12:00, including a simulated casualty in the water. Members of the public who see the exercise do not need to report it.

units.title: Advice to small craft: cold water
units.author: coast
units.text: Advice to small craft. Calm weather is tempting more people onto the water, but sea temperatures are now low enough for cold-water shock. Wear a lifejacket, carry a means of calling for help, tell someone ashore when you expect to be back, and return before dark.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 14th. Boat came at last, very late in the day, and the boatman would not lie alongside after dark but put off at once. Flour, oil, salt pork. The two men went off with it, and a third with them without leave, so now nine on the roll. Tally 30 stems, all on the near lines. Oil short again by the reckoning, lamps being kept as before.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 16th. Hard frost, no wind at all, the quietest night I have known here. Tally 19 stems. The foreman has the men sleep in the one hut now, for the warmth he says, & the other two are shut up. I keep the book by the lamp as ever. Wages to the 14th, all paid. Nine on the roll.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan 23. 00:00 wind E 2, visibility good, frost. 02:00 lamp checked. 03:00 lamp checked. Remarks: Assistant keeper's transfer approved, to take effect at the month end. A relief man is promised from Weyhaven. The road clear all watch. I have taken to drawing the kitchen curtain on the landward side, which I note only because I have never done so before.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day seven. Walked the whole east shore at low water. Gulls, oystercatchers, a pair of ravens on the north crag (Corvus, the usual). Otter spraint at the burn mouth: the only mammal sign apart from hares in a week. Browse line on the holly still unexplained. [Sketch: the burn mouth, tide line marked.] Boatman early, fidgeting with the painter. Told him tomorrow is my last day. He looked relieved.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 9. Wind back to east. Tam came round with a bottle and we sat by the stove. He said he wont fish the Holm side again this winter and he wont say why and I said then dont. Mother says her father was the same one winter and went back the next spring as if nothing. Lamp on all night. Paid the coal man.

units.title: Kittering Holm relay station (proposed, 1950s): summary
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: A lighthouse relay station on the Holm's south shoulder was proposed in the 1950s and surveyed in a single season. The survey report found the site suitable but recommended against it 'for reasons of staffing', without further explanation. The proposal was announced in the Courier and quietly dropped. Society holdings include the report and two letters [citation needed: the second letter's date is illegible].

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. 'For reasons of staffing' is a phrase this wiki is in danger of treating as a riddle. In the 1950s the lighthouse service could not keep keepers on rock stations with families on the mainland; nobody wanted a posting with a fortnightly boat. That is the reason. It is in every annual report of the period. This claim is well sourced, for once. Pell

units.title: Oral history project, Gilliver, 1974: tape 14 (one speaker)
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: INTERVIEWER: Did your family keep the lamp? SPEAKER: We did, and we didn't, if you follow. Dad wouldn't have it, said it was old wives. So Mother kept a candle in the back scullery where he'd not see it from the road. [laughs] Then he'd go and check it was lit before bed. Every night. Never said a word. That's men for you.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LBA-2219. Date: this month, day 29. Location: Brackwater reservoir, south dam. Kit: two omnidirectional mics, 30 cm spacing, gain 42 dB. Duration 45 min. Description: dawn chorus (robin, wren, blackbird with mimicry), geese overhead at 21:10, weir noise throughout. Percussive events: none. Curator's note: submitted by dunlin_rec; recorded in daylight.

units.title: Editor's note: a missing reel
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. Several readers have asked for the Courier's issues from the winter the Holm timber camp broke up. We must report that the microfilm reel for that winter, December to March, is missing from the archive. The index card is present and dated; the box is empty. This is not unusual for reels of that age, several of which were lent out in the 1960s and not returned.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: The paper's bound volumes for that winter were water-damaged in the 1953 flood and only the sports pages and advertisements survive. We have asked the national library whether it holds a copy. In the meantime we would be glad to hear from anyone with original issues from that winter in a loft or a drawer.

units.title: From the 'Gilliver Notes' column (undated, c. 1890s): the timber men
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The timber men are come home from the Holm before Christmas, which is earlier than looked for, and the village is glad to have them though they are in poor spirits and little inclined to talk. One remarked to your correspondent that the frost had 'got into the work'. The foreman is said to have paid all hands to the day. We wish them a better new year. (Your correspondent is told the camp broke up in January, not December; he records both dates.)

units.title: Scheduled notice: contract close, KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Scheduled notice. The final statement for site KH-01 will be issued after contract close. Timesheets for the final period must reach your operations manager by 23:59 on the last contract day. Year-end tax summaries will follow by post. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Your annual statement is ready
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Lyle Insurance. Your annual statement for policy LY-4471-0938 is ready to view. It shows the premiums paid this year and any claims made. Did you know? Many customers working away from home add our Remote Worker Extra for less than the price of a coffee a week. Peace of mind, wherever you are tonight. Small print: extension subject to acceptance.

units.title: Tell us about your remote site experience!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Tell us about your remote site experience! Our quick survey takes three minutes: 1) How many nights did you spend on site this season? 2) Rate your camp lighting from 1 to 5! 3) Did your camp ever feel too dark? 4) What would have made your nights easier? Every completed survey enters our draw for a Hearthglow Pro lantern, the brightest in the Sound!

units.title: Last chance! The Long Nights sale ends Sunday
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Last chance! The Long Nights sale ends this Sunday at midnight. Lanterns, spare mantles, rechargeable work lights and our bestselling solar fairy string, all reduced. Nights are drawing in fast, so don't get caught out! Plus: free delivery to Gilliver and Lisle on orders over 60 dollars until the end of the month.

units.title: Ammet Council weekly: bins, roads and your photos
units.author: council_news
units.text: Ammet Council weekly. Bins: collections are back to normal across the district; thank you for your patience. Roads: the Brackwater junction has reopened. Have your say: library opening hours consultation closes on the 12th. Photo competition: congratulations to our autumn winners, including 'Heron at Rope Walk'. Reminder: grit bins have been refilled for the cold spell.

units.title: A clarification regarding recent reports
units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: Further to our recent statement, Ardent Vale Holdings would like to clarify that we do not comment on our wider portfolio, which has been misrepresented in some recent reports. Each of our carefully chosen sites reflects the same long-term vision of patient, responsible stewardship. We have no plans to announce at this time, and we thank our partners for their continued discretion. The Ardent Vale community information team

units.title: Tomorrow's boat
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, for tomorrow: - Boat off Gilliver 06:30, at the landing about 07:15. - Everything that's going back to the depot on this run, please: chipper, spare saws, empties, waste. - Food for the 30th and 31st is on board, in case timings slip. - I still don't have crew transfer times. I'm chasing the client today. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A note from head office
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office asked me to pass this on, so I'm passing it on as written: if the clearance isn't complete at close on the 30th, the company will review options with the client. I don't know yet what that means in practice, and I would rather not guess in writing. Please get the final count to me on the 30th either way. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Your own saw
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, if any of the saws on site are your own rather than company kit, please label them clearly before anything goes on the boat. Everything that arrives at the depot unlabelled gets booked in as company plant, and I can't vouch for what happens to it after that. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll's account still shows wages outstanding this afternoon. I've told head office it's in hand. Please don't make me wrong about that. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Leaver's final timesheet
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll needs the leaver's last timesheet signed off by site before they can close the account properly. If it's somewhere in the cabin, a photo with tomorrow's empties is fine. Their family has rung the office to check the final pay, so I'd like to get it right first time. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, still no word from the client on transfer times. I'm sorry this is so late in the day. I'll write again tomorrow, early, whatever I have. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello, a short note. My piece on the end of the contract runs on the 30th. It says only what we can confirm, which is not much. If anything changes on your side after the 30th, my offer stands, with no deadline and no name attached. I hope everyone out there is well. Best wishes, Nell

units.title: Two trees walk into a bar
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. The barman says 'we don't serve your kind'. The trees say 'that's fine, we're leaving'. It's the leaving that's the joke, you see. Look, I said I'd forget the other thing and I have. But get Ruth to put the pick-up in writing. Times, boat, who. In writing. Anyway, the cabin's out of biscuits and morale is at an all-time low. Hal

units.title: which harbour?
units.author: sam
units.text: hi. Mum walked to the end of the garden today without the frame and then had to be helped back by the kid, who was extremely bossy about it. the dog went too, for moral support. anyway. she's asked if she can come to the harbour when you get back. I said I don't know which harbour, or when. I rang Grieve's office and a nice woman called Ruth said she'd let me know. so I'm waiting. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: sorry. I keep writing to you as if you're on the end of a phone. it's very quiet here tonight, no wind at all, you can hear the trains from the junction and a dog three gardens down. I hope it's quiet there too. the good kind of quiet. x

units.title: Not apologising this time
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, it's Ana. I won't apologise this time, because Tomas says I apologise too much. I'm fine. I made soup for my neighbour and she gave me a plant I don't know how to look after. If he's coming home after the 30th I'll be at the harbour, whichever one it is. Does anyone know which one? Is he sleeping? Ana
